questions.q: A Distributed Denial of Service (DDoS) attack works by:
options: Flooding a target server with traffic from many compromised machines
questions.solution: A botnet of 'zombie' systems swamps the target with requests so genuine users cannot be served. Nothing is encrypted (ransomware) or stolen directly - availability alone is attacked.
questions.shortcut: DDoS = Distributed (many machines) + Denial (availability lost).

questions.q: Which of the following is a markup language rather than a programming language?
questions.solution: HTML (HyperText Markup Language) only structures and presents content using tags; it has no logic/control-flow constructs of its own, so it is a markup language. Python, C++ and Java are programming languages.
questions.shortcut: Markup = tags for layout (HTML, XML, Markdown). If the option 'structures web pages', it is not a programming language.

questions.q: Which of the following areas characterises fifth-generation computers?
questions.solution: The 5th generation targets AI, natural-language processing, parallel and quantum-style computing. Punched cards belong to the pre-1st/1st era, assembly is a 2nd-generation language habit, and vacuum tubes are 1st generation.
questions.shortcut: Anything with 'intelligence, learning, robotics, parallel' = 5th generation.

questions.q: The default port number for HTTPS traffic is:
questions.solution: HTTPS runs over TLS on port 443; 80 is plain HTTP, 21 is FTP control, 8080 is a common alternate proxy port.
questions.shortcut: 443 = the padlock port.

questions.q:
Select the option that can substitute the given group of words.

That which cannot be avoided
questions.solution: Cannot be avoided = **inevitable**. Link each option to its verb: conquer→invincible, see→invisible, believe→incredible. The stem's verb ('avoided') picks its partner.
questions.shortcut: Verb-link: avoid → inevitable.

questions.q:
Select the most appropriate option to substitute the highlighted segment in the given sentence. If no substitution is required, select 'No substitution required'.

The quality of the mangoes **were** not satisfactory this season.
questions.solution: The subject is **quality**; 'of the mangoes' is an interrupter → quality **was** not satisfactory. 'Have been' and 'are being' repeat the plural fault.
questions.shortcut: cover the 'of' phrase; quality is singular.

questions.q: Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number (1).
questions.solution: The exchange scheme is the *cause* of the change: because every plastic bag was swapped for a cloth one, visitors stopped bringing plastic at all. The main clause ('visitors slowly gave up…') is the direct result of the scheme, so **Because** fits. *Although* would claim the scheme did not stop them — yet the visitors asked for the cloth bags themselves, which is the scheme working, not failing.
questions.shortcut: Ask: is the main clause the working of the first clause (because) or a surprise against it (although)?
questions.passage: The hill temple at Pachaimalai banned plastic bags five years ago, and the change began at the gate. (1) ______ the staff exchanged a cloth bag for every plastic one handed over at the gate, visitors slowly gave up carrying plastic altogether. (2) ______ the ban, monkeys used to scatter torn plastic along the paths; the slopes are clean now, and pilgrims often photograph them. The ban has even spread beyond the temple; (3) ______, the village panchayat passed a similar rule for its weekly market.

questions.q:
Select the option that expresses the given sentence in indirect speech.

She said to me, "I will meet you tomorrow."
options: She told me that she will meet me the next day.
She told me that she would meet you the next day.
She said me that she would meet me the next day.
She told me that she would meet me the next day.
questions.solution: said to me → told me; will → **would**; you → **me** (listener); tomorrow → **the next day**. B skips the backshift; C leaves 'you' unconverted; D writes the impossible 'said me'.
questions.shortcut: Four checks: told + would + me + next day.

questions.q: Sarnath was inscribed as a UNESCO World Heritage Site in —
questions.solution: Sarnath — where the Buddha preached his first sermon — was designated a World Heritage Site on 25 July 2026.
questions.shortcut: Sarnath = first-sermon site, listed July 2026.

questions.q: A 100 W bulb glows for 10 hours. How much electrical energy does it consume?
questions.solution: Energy = power × time = 100 W × 10 h = 1,000 Wh = **1 kWh** (1 unit).

questions.q: The Urdu weekly ***Al-Hilal*** (1912) was started by —
questions.solution: **Maulana Abul Kalam Azad** launched *Al-Hilal* from Calcutta in 1912. Mohammad Ali Jauhar edited *Comrade*.
questions.shortcut: **A**l-Hilal → **A**zad.

questions.q: Which of the following is a rabi crop?
questions.solution: **Mustard** is sown in October–November and harvested in March–April, so it is a **rabi** crop, like wheat, barley and gram. Paddy, jute and cotton are monsoon-sown **kharif** crops.
questions.shortcut: Winter-sown = rabi; the other three need monsoon water.

questions.q: In a class of 60 students, 65% are boys. The number of girls in the class is:
questions.shortcut: 35% of 60 = 21. (39 is the number of boys — the trap.)

questions.q: Simplify: $60 \div 5 \times 3 - 18 \div 6 \times 2 + 7$
questions.shortcut: Trap 25 comes from multiplying before dividing ($60 \div 15 = 4$).

questions.q: What is 35% of 480?
A sum of money becomes 1.44 times itself in 2 years when invested at compound interest. The annual rate of interest is:
questions.shortcut: √1.44 = 1.2 ⇒ rate 20%. (14.4% is the trap for linear thinking.)

questions.q: What is the minimum number of straight lines needed to draw the given figure?
questions.solution: Grid: 5 vertical + 5 horizontal = 10. The two long diagonals run corner to corner: 2 more. Total = **12**.

questions.q: In an examination, **35% of candidates failed in Mathematics, 25% failed in English and 10% failed in both**. If **250 candidates passed in both** subjects, how many candidates appeared?
questions.solution: Failed at least one = 35 + 25 − 10 = 50%, so passed both = 50%. Total = 250 × 100 ÷ 50 = **500**. 625 comes from 100 − 35 − 25 = 40%, which forgets to add back the 10% who failed both.
questions.shortcut: Passed both = 100 − (fail₁ + fail₂ − fail both).

questions.q: How many triangles are there in the given figure?
questions.figure: <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 130 130" width="130" height="130" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.5" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round"><line x1="5" y1="125" x2="125" y2="125"/><line x1="65" y1="5" x2="125" y2="125"/><line x1="5" y1="125" x2="65" y2="5"/><line x1="5" y1="125" x2="95" y2="65"/><line x1="35" y1="65" x2="125" y2="125"/><line x1="65" y1="5" x2="65" y2="125"/></svg>
questions.solution: All three medians meet at one centre point and make 6 smallest triangles. Two-piece triangles (a full side as base, the centre as top): 3. Three-piece triangles (each median cuts the big one into two halves): 6. The whole triangle: 1. Total = 6 + 3 + 6 + 1 = **16**.
questions.shortcut: Triangle with 3 medians = 16 (memorise).

questions.q:
**Statement:** A few students of a college were caught copying in the final examination.

**Courses of action:**
I. The results of all students of the college should be cancelled.
II. Action should be taken against those caught and invigilation should be made stricter.

Which of the courses of action follow(s)?
options: Only course of action I follows
Only course of action II follows
questions.solution: I punishes honest students for the fault of a few — **does not follow**. II acts on the wrongdoers and prevents a repeat — **follows**. Answer: **only II**.
questions.shortcut: Act against the few who did wrong, not against everyone.
